memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium. Computacenter (CCC-GB) at 5,470p on 2026-10-01 is a crisp 'Demand Inflection' in a well-run but structurally low-margin reseller whose inflection the market has already paid for: the 'Modal return' is 1.2 percent a year over eighteen months (to 2028-04-01; value including cash returns 5,572p) and 5.2 percent a year over three years (to 2029-10-01; 6,370p) against the 20% bar, an F. The park is on price, not quality: the park rule's four gates do not trigger (management A; business quality B; predictability B; trackability C). Progress to an Early-Stage record at or below about 4,240p (the eighteen-month entry level, 22% below the reference price, close to the 150-day average of 4,243.7p), or earlier if the FY2026 results in March 2027 show North American gross margin stable above 8%, second-half free cash flow conversion above 80% of adjusted operating profit, the backlog above £9.3bn and the largest customer's share of revenue falling, with the multiple below 16x. The view is bullish on the business, neutral on the stock, bearish on the price. On the drop-through sensitivity the entry level falls to about 3,790p.
case: - The change is external, sector-level and as strong as any force in the universe. Hyperscaler AI infrastructure capital expenditure is projected at $1.5tr in 2027 (Morgan Stanley); Nvidia's supply shortfall is about $100bn; Dell's AI-optimised server growth 757%; Bechtle's backlog a record €3.5bn. The force meets every part of the framework's 'Demand Inflection' test and has shown up in the company's own numbers: committed backlog £9.3bn at 30-Jun-26 (+323.2%), about a year of FY2025 revenue, running into FY2027; North America 62% of adjusted operating profit from 44%; the company's own cycle turned from H1 2024 -13.4% to H1 2026 +71.6%. External forces A; Demand A; Revenue cycle A. Direction by force: demand strong tailwind; competition mildly tightening (Softcat into US sourcing); disruption two-sided (software agency models erode reselling; liquid-cooled GPU complexity favours integrators, B); political and regulatory a European tailwind (German procurement reform 14-Feb-26; EU sovereignty package 3-Jun-26; NIS2 and DORA, B); supply side a headwind on margin and timing and a tailwind on share (C); macro mixed, acting differently rather than more (strong dollar flatters 62% of profit; rising rates cost on £860m of working capital, C). Catch-all B: Jefferies' second phase of AI spending (token optimisation) would shift demand toward integration and advisory.

- The internal change is the company doing what it has always done, a little faster: Internal forces C. Four of twelve screen forces at moderate strength: Guidance raised A (FY2026 floor to no less than £380m, more than 30% above the market's starting point of about £290m); Acquisitions B (AgreeYa 8.5x, GAI 11.5x; integration proceeding as planned; not A because US ERP integrations took up to five years against 18 months); New geographies B (GAI's US federal route, zero customer overlap; North America itself); Perimeter reduction B (hosting exits; Switzerland folded into Germany; BT Services costs reduced); Standards B (central costs raised to fund productivity; CRM; cloud ERP in design; provisions raised; the ERP history the caution); Strategy C (unchanged, resourced, scale changed); New products C (liquid-cooled rack staging; offshore services); Balance sheet C (used harder for working capital, not by choice); Shareholder returns C (progressive; distributable reserves restored by a £260.8m intercompany dividend February 2026); Other leaders C (Mortimer, a 25-year insider, CFO; Jehle left December 2024 and joined Bechtle); Chief executive D (no change; Jefferies named a 2026 successor announcement as a catalyst; none in the files); Price rises D (cost-plus and agency; gross margin down 303 basis points; the one exception North American Services +1,888 basis points); Catch-all C (the deliberate acceptance of lower percentage margin for higher absolute gross profit, the choice the counter-case attacks). No screen red flag fires.

- 'Financial Outputs' B: layers 4 to 6 all moved decisively (backlog, revenue, operating profit, EPS, guidance, consensus) while margin and cash moved the wrong way as the price of growth. Key metrics B under the framework's conditional rule (near term very positive, FY2026 consensus EPS +47.3%, so continuation logic suffices: backlog, Atlanta, acquisitions, German recovery): Revenue growth A (the rate stepped up against each of the last three years; the base business grew 13% without North America against market growth of 8%); Margin D (adjusted EBIT margin 5.2% FY2021 to 3.0% FY2025 to 2.2% H1 2026; conversion 24% against a 30% target; not F because absolute profit nearly doubled); Cash conversion D (193% of net income FY2024, 130% FY2025, negative H1 2026; the 80% H2 2026 test adopted as a leading indicator); Net debt B (no debt problem; net funds £308.7m). Goldilocks growth C (outside the band at every horizon: six months about +29% on H2 2026 EPS of about 158p against 122.6p; eighteen months 27.6% a year compounded but the second year about 10%; three years about 8% a year from the FY2026 base, 2.60 to 3.30 GBP; the three-year rate from FY2025 about 20% but almost all FY2026). Sell-side upgrades B (further upgrades probable but smaller; consensus 383 GBPm already above the £380m floor): Dashboard revisions A; Revision skew A (all eight brokers raised FY2026 and FY2027; FY2027 mean up 16.1% in one month, 30.5% in three, 43.0% in twelve; range 1.94 to 2.80 GBP, latest the high; the only trim Rothschild & Co Redburn's March 2026 tax cut); Modal forecast B (2.60 GBP above the floor and consensus; H2 the heavier half; floor beaten in three of four years); Guidance vs consensus B; Guidance conservatism B (disciplined sandbaggers; Jefferies FY2026 261p 15% above pre-results Visible Alpha 227.2p; FY2027 272p 6% above 256.9p; Morgan Stanley reads the floor as saying prior consensus was far too low; dispersion wide, FY2027 EPS 2.64 to 3.05 GBP, revenue 13,829 to 18,041 GBPm); Upgrade record B (FY2020 upgraded twice above £190m; FY2021 £255.6m beat; FY2024 missed, breaking 19 years of EPS growth, adjusted pre-tax profit -8.6%, first half 17% below consensus; FY2025 £272m 6% ahead; FY2026 raised April, July, September). Staircase B: near steps B (peers' Q3 statements late October to early November 2026; Hatfield completion 2026; possible succession announcement; FY2026 results with H2 cash conversion and North American margin disclosures); mid steps B (Atlanta mid-2027; AgreeYa US integration H1 2027; first full GAI year; German stimulus; H1 2027 results September 2027); far steps C (ERP migration, cash drag peaking FY2026; backlog phasing into FY2028; £500m-plus of incremental gross profit from the acquisitions by 2028 treated as an upper bound).
counter_case: - At the whole-case level, in its strongest form: the H1 2026 numbers are the top of a hyperscaler capital-expenditure cycle whose participants now spend more than their operating cash flow and whose next year may stall after a doubling in 2026, on Jefferies' own semiconductor team's warning. Computacenter's growth within that cycle is concentrated to a degree the company does not disclose: one customer was £2,731.2m, nearly 30% of FY2025 group revenue, and 85% of FY2025 US revenue growth came from one client. The company bought that growth with its margin (gross margin 9.6%, down 303 basis points; operating margin on revenue 2.2%) and its balance sheet (inventory £1.26bn from £316.8m; net operating cash outflow £82.6m; net funds £308.7m from £606.0m). The parts that would normally bound the downside, a sticky European services base and a 94% renewal rate, are the parts that are shrinking (Services revenue -1.7% constant currency; UK Services gross margin -706 basis points; provisions £24.8m). If the largest customer pauses, revenue, margin and cash reverse together, the shares revert to the sector's 12x to 14x on lower earnings, and the loss from 5,470p is 30% to 40%; the pre-results bear case of 1,550p at 8.0x on 161.6p shows how far this stock has been valued at the bottom of a cycle. Softcat's $1.05bn purchase of GDT says the US early-mover advantage has a shelf life. The record concedes the concentration, undisclosed and large; the margin direction; the shape of the cash flow; the stale bound on the downside; and that the return from here is poor even if none of this happens. It does not concede the false-friend frame: the half delivered a near-doubling of operating profit with North American services margins up 1,888 basis points, the services decline is a chosen exit, and the inventory is customer-backed (the H1 2025 outflow of £165.8m reversed into FY2025 free cash flow of £206.9m). The forces and the outputs are real; the price is the problem.

- At 'Foundations': the integration-centre advantage is a moat only while hardware is complex; hyperscalers can and will transact directly with OEMs for standardised racks; the company is a warehouse and working-capital provider to its largest customers (£137.7m of inventory in one customer's facility; £100m of early customer prepayments; unbilled receivable days 9.6%, the highest in the peer set). Conceded in full on the working-capital evidence; held off for two to three years by liquid cooling, high-density racks and allocation scarcity; live beyond that, and the reason the Value Chain and Industry Element is C not B.
triggers: - Entry: progress at or below about 4,240p (eighteen-month entry level on the modal path; about 3,690p on the three-year path; about 3,790p on the drop-through sensitivity).

- FY2026 results (mid-March 2027; block 2027-03-17, review February 2027): progress earlier if North American gross margin is stable above 8%, H2 2026 free cash flow conversion above 80% of adjusted operating profit, the backlog above £9.3bn and the largest customer's share of revenue falling, with the multiple below 16x. Alarm: backlog below £9.3bn; invalidate: backlog below £7.1bn. Alarm: North American gross margin below 8%; invalidate: below 7.5%. Alarm: conversion below 23%. Alarm: H2 2026 cash conversion below 80%; invalidate: a second consecutive half of operating cash outflow. Alarm: largest customer above 30% of revenue at FY2026. Alarm: provisions above £30m; any UK or German Managed Services organic decline above 5% in a half with Technology Sourcing growing above 20%.

- Demand side: a cut to any large hyperscaler's capital-expenditure guidance would change the first side taken (about 65% that demand holds through 2027). Peers' Q3 statements (Bechtle, Softcat; late October to early November 2026): similar double-digit order-book growth means a rising tide rather than share capture and a de-rated premium. Nvidia and Dell AI-server shipments quarterly. Jefferies' semiconductor team's 2027 stall warning.

- Margin and cash: North American gross margin below 7.5% or conversion below 23% at FY2026 changes the second side (about 50% that the margin stabilises). A second consecutive half of operating cash outflow changes the third (about 70% that H2 2026 converts above 80%).

- The multiple: FY2027 consensus above 3.00 GBP with the multiple still at 18x after the FY2026 results would say the market has decided the growth is structural; the 'Compounder' reading then deserves a second look. The chance of the multiple at or above 18.9x at eighteen months is about 25%.
- Organic Services revenue growth double-digit by the FY2027 interims (September 2027) is the sell-side's services test; alarm if not met.
